plan: Represent the workspace as a deep-copied nested dict tree; sections and groups are the only container kinds, mirroring crates holding parcels and smaller crates.
Implement one recursive traversal generator (_walk) yielding (item, level) pairs, and drive word counting, marker collection, and outline rendering uniformly from it.
Count note words by removing [[?identifier]] marker tokens first, then matching \b\w+\b; add references' declared word_count; aggregate recursively over the whole tree.
Collect unresolved identifiers from note marker tokens and reference unresolved lists into a set, returned sorted lexicographically.
Render the outline deterministically: workspace title, then '<kind>: <title>' per item with two spaces per nesting level, in list order.

Implement move as validate-then-mutate: check id types, item existence, destination container-ness, self/descendant containment, and index range before any list mutation, so a failed move leaves to_data() unchanged.
Return deep copies from to_data() so callers cannot mutate internal state.
mechanisms: composite tree of dict nodes with container kinds {section, group}
single recursive traversal generator shared by all query operations
recursive aggregation for total word count with marker-stripped regex word matching
set-based marker collection with sorted deterministic output
level-tracking pre-order traversal for indented outline rendering
containment invariant check (non-container destination and self/descendant cycle rejection)
atomic move: full validation before any mutation, then remove-and-insert
